rules.source: RFC 0003 §4.4 F9, F10; RC1-50; review L1 of #1200; #1215; review L4 of #1231
rules.statement: The periodic revalidation cannot be turned off or left unbounded: `cosec.authorization.snapshot.revalidate-interval` is at least 1 second, at most 5 minutes and, with fail-closed tenants, less than `fail-closed.max-lag`, or startup fails naming it (the lag thresholds are 6 and 30 intervals, `SNP-23`, so it is always below them). Installed documents are revalidated by periodic passes, each a conditional read of the store per document, never a local copy, and a reset of the change channel reloads them all. A pass starts every interval or, when the previous one is still in flight, as soon as it ends. A change written to the store before a pass starts, whose invalidation was lost or whose reload failed, is installed by the time that pass has finished with its document, whether or not a load of that document was in flight when the pass reached it: a pass never counts as its confirmation a store read that began before the pass did. It joins a load in flight only if that load started after the pass did; otherwise it waits for one more load after it, whose read is the pass's. A pass that has finished no document for `storeReadTimeout` and has no read in flight is abandoned at the next tick; a pass with a read in flight never is. A pass does not wait for a load of a document that has been in flight longer than `storeReadTimeout`; if that load started before the pass did, one more load still follows it, so the change is installed once that load's compilation ends, never only at a later pass.

rules.statement: A snapshot document's header is read from its body: the stored bytes are the whole document, and the only way to make a SnapshotDocument is SnapshotDocuments, which reads schema, revision and publishedAt from them (read) or from the document it encodes (of). rules.source: RFC 0013 B2b (the family bound under a burst)
rules.statement: A family holds at most its bound plus the smaller of its bound and 4,096 entries of each kind (documents; entries for documents the store does not hold), plus the entries being installed or loaded at that moment; an install that finds its kind over that evicts at most 64 entries of that kind on the installing thread before it answers its waiters, which takes it back within the cap, and housekeeping evicts the rest. Evictions never take a kind below its bound, and passes running at once leave a kind at its bound when every victim was idle: they never stop above it.

rules.statement: What a spent drain budget leaves is not left waiting on the compile queue. An event the source's own work produces (a read's answer, failure or timeout, a compilation's result, an effect's failure, a retry coming due) is taken by the thread that holds the key's flag or the next one to take it, before any budget check and uncounted. A caller event left by a spent budget is handed to the source's own threads, where it waits for at most the compilation a pool thread is running; when the pool refuses it housekeeping runs it, and when that refuses too, its offerer does.

rules.source: #1534 (what housekeeping refuses); RFC 0013 B2b (the runner's paths)
rules.statement: No thread that calls the snapshot source writes a log line, or runs housekeeping's work, because housekeeping's queue is full: a refused log line, eviction pass under the cap or lag report is dropped and counted by its task (`HousekeepingTask`), and housekeeping itself writes one summary at most every 10 seconds, only when something moved, naming the last text dropped per task without its stack. Only the over-cap pass (SNP-14), an empty key's drop and the source's hand-offs (SNP-15) run in place. A meter that throws is counted in the summary's own state, never logged on the caller's thread nor offered to housekeeping, and the summary is written whatever the metrics are. Housekeeping stopped by close is refusal too, except on the source's own threads, where the task runs in place uncounted; close ends by writing what was refused and not yet summarized, once, on the closing thread, whatever the interval.

rules.statement: A load's compilation has the load's deadline: one that has not answered when coldLoadTimeout (cold) or storeReadTimeout (reload) since the load began is spent ends the load as a failure by the next periodic tick (a cold load fails, a reload keeps what is installed, a recompile fails closed); a queued compilation of an ended load never starts, and a revision whose compilation timed out and still runs is not compiled again while it runs. A recompile that does not answer within its deadline leaves the document's validity under the new platform document unknown, so it fails closed; one the full compile queue refuses is a matter of capacity, and keeps what is installed for at most coldLoadTimeout since its load began (SNP-4).

rules.source: maintainer decision 2026-11-22 (what can be computed is not configured); the properties review, items 1-4, 7
rules.statement: What a snapshot source's options once took as settings is computed, from the revalidation interval, the pipeline's timeout and the machine, and the starter has no property for it: a document unconfirmed for 6 revalidation intervals is logged at WARN and for 30 at ERROR as stale, so a lag report is a count of missed passes and the warning threshold is always above the interval; a cold load waits 40 % of `cosec.pipeline.timeout` (never below a millisecond), so it never waits as long as the request it serves; the compile threads are one per 4 cores, between 1 and 4; a revalidation pass confirms 16 documents at once. A key that once set one (`lag-warn`, `lag-escalate`, `cold-load-timeout`, `compile-threads`, `reload-concurrency`, `shadow.report-interval`, and the control plane's keys of `CTL-72`) fails startup as a key CoSec does not read, saying it is no longer a property and what replaced it. The starter says once at startup what it derived and from what.
